info.title: Cumulus Talos API
info.description: Build, run and evaluate agents over cloud and phone. Every request carries an API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`); operations marked for idempotency also carry an `Idempotency-Key`.

post.description:
Create an agent from a template. The response includes its first draft; publish a version before running it.

Choose `phone_outbound` for outgoing calls, `cloud_task` for a task, `cloud_chat` for a chat or `blank` for an empty flow.

Read the agent ID from `ref.id` and the first draft’s ID and revision from `draft`. Edit with `drafts_edit`, then check the result with `drafts_validate`.

patch.description:
Apply typed edits to a draft in order. Send the revision you last read to prevent overwriting another editor’s changes.

Send `{draft_id, expected_revision, edits}`. Edits are typed and applied in order. Read node IDs from `drafts_get`.

Common edits include:

- `agent.telephony` with `value: {trunkId, from}`.
- `flow.prompt` with `text` for the global prompt.
- `node.instruction` with `component_id`, `node_id` and `instruction: {type: "prompt" | "static_text", text}`; use `component_id: null` for the main flow.
- `agent.settings` with `values` and `clear`.
- `agent.provider` with `role` (`llm`, `stt` or `tts`) and `changes`.
- `notification.put` with the signed webhook configuration.

For incoming caller context, define a dedicated phone `POST` action with `action.put`, `effect_key` idempotency and `timeout_ms` at most 10000. Bind it with `phone.inbound_context` and `value: {action_id, variables: ["customer_name", "noCallerIdMatch"]}`. The action runs before speech, receives `{event: "call_inbound", call_inbound: {agent_id, agent_version, from_number, to_number}}` and returns `{call_inbound: {dynamic_variables: string_map, reject?: boolean}}`.

An existing Retell-verified endpoint can use `auth.scheme: "retell_signature"` with a pinned `http_auth` secret. Other HTTP authentication schemes are also supported. Set the context binding’s `value` to null to remove it.

A validation diagnostic’s `fixes[].edits` can be submitted as draft edits against the revision you validated.

Compile a draft and read its diagnostics, next version number and digest. Resolve error diagnostics before publishing.

Send `{draft_id, expected_revision}`. The response includes `ok`, `version`, `digest` and `diagnostics`. Use the returned `version` when publishing. Set `include_plan: true` to also receive the compiled public plan for review when validation succeeds.

When `ok` is false, resolve the error diagnostics. If a diagnostic supplies `fixes[].edits`, apply them with `drafts_edit` against the validated revision, then validate again. `telephony_*` warnings explain why a phone call would be refused.

post.description:
Compile a draft into an immutable version. Set live: false to create a test version; the default makes it live for new runs.

Use the `version` returned by `drafts_validate`.

- `live: false` creates a test publication and keeps the live head unchanged. Run it with `test_runs_create`, then promote it with `publications_promote`.
- `live: true` is the default and makes the publication live immediately.
- `keep_draft: true` keeps the working draft open for further edits.

post.description:
Import a Retell conversation-flow export into a draft. Review diagnostics and test the imported behavior before publishing.

Inspect the export with `agents_import_inspect` first. Only conversation-flow exports are accepted.

- Set `flow` to the export’s `conversationFlow`. Put the remaining export in `agent`, with `version` equal to `agent_version` and `agent_name` set.
- Set `reference` to `{tenant_id, kind: "agent", id}`. Read the current tenant from `environments_list`; use a new agent ID or the existing draft target.
- Replacing unpublished draft changes requires `replace_draft: {draft_id, expected_revision}`. Otherwise the import returns `409` with reason `draft_has_changes`. The live publication is unchanged.
- Set `agent.webhook_url` to null unless `config.webhook` pins the same URL.
- Select the LLM from `models_list`: `llm: {provider: "openai", model: {model_id, provider, tier}}`. Choose speech settings from `voices_list`: `stt: {provider: "elevenlabs", model: "scribe_v2_realtime"}` and `tts: {provider: "elevenlabs", model, voiceId}`.
- Set `config.recording` to `{required: true, channels: "dual"}`. Leave out `config.telephony` until the trunk and number exist.
- For each `model_binding_required` diagnostic, map its path in `model_bindings` to `{model: {model_id, provider, tier}}`.

Use `allow_blocked: true` to keep a structurally valid draft with publication blockers, including privacy settings. `result.validation` reports those blockers and may be absent on an unchanged replay. Inline credentials and malformed sources are still refused. Validate again before publishing; this option does not bypass publication or admission checks.

Retell voices, languages outside `en`/`es` and knowledge bases do not carry over. A new import returns `201`; importing the same body onto its unedited draft returns `200`.

post.description:
Start a cloud task, chat or phone call from a published agent. The response confirms admission; follow the run to determine its outcome.

For a phone call, send `{channel: "phone", agent_id, to, from, dynamic_variables}` and optionally `version`. The request dials a real number, including with `test: true`; confirm the destination before calling. Test runs are excluded from billing, customer webhooks and event triggers.

Use an imported number for `from`, or omit it to use the publication’s `telephony.from`. Supply the flow’s required variables in `dynamic_variables`; missing inputs return `missing_dynamic_variables`.

Check these refusal reasons:

- `tenant_not_configured` or `tenant_disabled`: ask Cumulus to configure capacity and open admission.
- `trunk_not_authorized`: check that the caller ID and trunk are authorized.
- `capacity_exhausted`: wait for concurrent-run capacity.

For cloud execution, send `{channel: "cloud", agent_id, mode: "task" | "chat", input}`. To chat with a phone agent without dialing, use cloud chat with `test: true`.

put.description:
Create a secret or add a version. Keep the returned version for references in agents and trunks; the response does not return the value.

Use an admin key. Choose `sip_auth` for a trunk password, `webhook_signing` for a webhook secret or `http_auth` for an HTTP credential. The response returns metadata, never the value. Reference the saved secret as `{id, version: current_version}`.

For a Basis Theory proxy credential, use `http_auth` and an `action.put` edit with `auth: {scheme: "header", header_name: "BT-PROXY-KEY", secret_ref: {id, version}}`. Remove the key query parameter from the action URL and keep the value out of prompts. Proxy access does not grant tokenization permissions.

Enable inbound on the Twilio trunk and configure its returned `inbound_sip_uri` in Twilio Origination first.

Setting `inbound_agent_id` pins the agent’s current publication and the assigning admin’s live authority to the number. Each signed SIP arrival admits an inbound run. Set the field to null to remove the assignment; reassign after publishing or promoting a new version.

post.description:
Connect your carrier’s SIP trunk using a versioned credential secret. Enable inbound routing if the trunk will receive calls.

Use an admin key and configure call capacity with Cumulus first. `tenant_not_configured` means that setup is missing.

1. Store the SIP password with `secrets_put`, using `kind: "sip_auth"`.
2. Pass `auth_secret: {id, version: current_version}` to connect the trunk.
3. For Twilio, set `termination_uri` to the Termination host (`<name>.pstn.twilio.com`) and enable Secure Trunking. Calls use TLS and SRTP.
4. For incoming calls, set `inbound: true` and configure the returned `inbound_sip_uri` as Twilio’s Origination URI with secure trunking enabled.
5. Import the numbers and assign a published phone agent.

post.description:
Create simulation cases with caller behavior, assertions and action mocks for an agent.

Set `spec.kind` to `simulation` and define `cases`. Each case needs a lowercase-slug `case_id`, name, caller and assertions. Add dynamic variables, HTTP action mocks and an optional trial count.

Choose a caller with either `{kind: "persona", goal, brief}` or `{kind: "script", steps: [{says}]}`. Assertion IDs are your labels; node IDs come from `drafts_get` or `publications_get`.

Deterministic assertions include `node_visited`, `node_not_visited`, `final_node`, `path`, `agent_says`, `tool_called`, `variable`, `ended`, `transfer` and `disposition`. For `agent_says`, use `expect: "never" | "at_least_once"` and `match: {patterns}`. A `rubric` assertion uses a model judge.

Mocks answer customer HTTP actions by `action_id`. An unmocked customer HTTP action fails with `unmocked_action` before sending; built-in actions have simulated defaults. Run the suite with `test_runs_create`.

JsonValue.description: Any JSON value: null, boolean, number, string, array or object.

ModelPolicyValue.description: A model data-policy value: any JSON value.

media_url.description: Direct signed URL of the recording bytes, for your own clients to read the audio (for example to draw a waveform): valid for at most five minutes and pinned to the recorded version. Do not share it; read runs.recording again for a fresh one when it expires
